decisions.reason: The candidate already refers to the approved Hero V rather than a superseded fixed silhouette, and its same-message MODIFY independently captures the newly specified literal-terminal derivation.
Its existing relationship remains valid because it generically derives the second V from the Hero V geometry and does not retain a conflicting reference to the rejected presentation version.
The selected Hero V silhouette does not invalidate any terminal-treatment attribute, and the candidate's same-message MODIFY already records the unified terminal gesture across all three forms.
Selecting the earlier Option 2 Hero V as the geometry foundation does not change the candidate's high-level brand character, positioning, or expression constraints.
The source selects a Hero V silhouette for the V system but does not resume or change the deferred construction requirements for the remaining proprietary letterforms.
The geometry-reference change leaves the deferred champagne-metal material requirements and the geometry-before-finish hierarchy unchanged.
The source does not resume or modify the deferred complete-wordmark rhythm, kerning, or visual-hierarchy requirements.
Changing the approved Hero V silhouette does not alter the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The Hero V geometry selection does not change the requirement to deliver final production-ready artwork.
